_comment: Ground truth for the review evals. Each fixture declares the defects deliberately planted
in it and the decoys that must NOT be reported. Line numbers are 1-indexed and refer to
the file as committed; a finding counts as a hit if it lands within `tolerance` lines of
the planted line, because a reviewer naming the function rather than the exact statement
Decoys matter as much as the planted defects. A reviewer that reports everything has
perfect recall and is worthless, and the failure mode of an eager model is noise rather
than blindness. clean.py has no planted defects at all: every finding there is a false
positive, which is the only way to measure precision without ambiguity.

planted.what: username is concatenated into the SQL string, so any quote in it changes the query

decoys.why_not_a_bug: the role value is bound as a parameter; the concatenation is of a constant empty string
string concatenation into a log label is not injection

planted.what: range stops at len-size, so a trailing partial chunk is silently dropped

decoys.why_not_a_bug: negative slicing is guarded by n > 0 and behaves correctly

planted.what: the file handle is not closed when the ValueError is raised; only the happy path closes it

decoys.why_not_a_bug: the with-statement closes the handle on every path
this file is correct throughout; any finding at all is a false positive
